title: Global Medical Response expands Bell fleet with additional Bell 407GXis
summary: These new aircraft will support GMR’s helicopter air ambulance fleet, enhancing access to critical care for patients in rural and metropolitan communities.
body_markdown:
Bell Textron Inc., announced during the annual Air Medical Transport Conference (AMTC) the purchase order for additional Bell 407GXis by Global Medical Response (GMR).


These new aircraft will support GMR’s helicopter air ambulance (HAA) fleet, enhancing access to critical care for patients in rural and metropolitan communities alike.


“GMR is recognized around the world for delivering high-quality, time-sensitive emergency medical services, and we are honored that they continue to place their trust in Bell,” said Danny Maldonado, president and CEO, Bell.


“The[407GXi](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/bell/407gxi) ’s combination of reliability, speed, and efficiency makes it an ideal platform for air medical operators. We are proud to support GMR’s life-saving missions and the crews who rely on Bell aircraft every day.”


GMR is the nation’s largest EMS provider, operating an extensive network of air and ground assets that provide critical and prehospital care to communities across the United States.


GMR’s air medical teams connect patients with the advanced care they need, often serving rural and hard-to-reach areas where rapid access is essential. GMR operates the largest Bell HAA fleet with more than 170 Bell aircraft supporting emergency medical missions nationwide.


“Every minute matters when a patient needs critical care,” said GMR president and chief operating officer Ted Van Horne.


“The Bell[407GXi](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/bell/407gxi) strengthens our ability to deliver advanced critical care when and where patients need it most. Its proven reliability, modern avionics, and IFR capability enhance operational safety, improve mission reliability, and expand patient access during forecasted or unforeseen weather conditions. By increasing our IFR-capable fleet, we are extending our ability to reach more patients, serve more communities, and provide dependable access to lifesaving care when weather or distance might otherwise limit our response. This investment reflects our continued commitment to safety, clinical excellence, and operational readiness.”


The[Bell 407GXi](https://www.bellflight.com/products/bell-407) is a proven, multi-mission helicopter widely utilized for[HAA services](https://www.bellflight.com/missions/hems-helicopters) around the world. Featuring the Garmin G1000H NXi avionics suite and IFR capability, the aircraft combines enhanced situational awareness, strong hot-and-high performance, and fuel efficiency.


Its versatile cabin and wide-access doors support the rapid loading and unloading of patients and medical equipment, making it well suited for time-sensitive air medical transport.


To find out more about how the Bell[407GXi](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/bell/407gxi) advances missions worldwide, visit the Bell product[page](https://www.bellflight.com/products/bell-407) , or stop by Bell booth #617 during[AMTC 2026](https://www.bellflight.com/events/amtc) .


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Bell.*
